name: Section
text: THE PROBLEM

name: Slide title
text:
Flight needed control,
not just lift
textPreview: Flight needed control, | not just lift

name: Slide description
text: A machine could rise into the air. The harder problem was keeping it balanced and steering it safely.
textPreview: A machine could rise into the air. The harder problem was keeping it balanced and steering it safely.

alt: The Wright brothers studying a model glider in their workshop

text: Historical context: The Wright brothers approached flight as a control problem as well as a problem of lift and power. Source: National Park Service, Wright Brothers, https://www.nps.gov/articles/wright-brothers.htm

name: Section
text: THE EXPERIMENTS

name: Slide title
text:
They learned by
flying gliders

name: Slide description
text: At Kitty Hawk, repeated glides gave Wilbur and Orville practical flying skill and exposed what their designs could not yet do.
textPreview: At Kitty Hawk, repeated glides gave Wilbur and Orville practical flying skill and exposed what their designs could not yet do.

alt: A Wright glider in a test flight above the Kitty Hawk dunes

text: The brothers conducted extensive glider experiments at the Outer Banks before powered flight. Source: National Park Service, The First Flight, https://www.nps.gov/wrbr/learn/historyculture/thefirstflight.htm

name: Section
text: THE BREAKTHROUGH

name: Slide title
text:
A wind tunnel turned
guesswork into data
textPreview: A wind tunnel turned | guesswork into data

name: Slide description
text: Their own tests showed that published lift figures were unreliable. A small wind tunnel let them compare wing shapes and design with evidence.
textPreview: Their own tests showed that published lift figures were unreliable. A small wind tunnel let them compare wing shapes and design with evid...

alt: The Wright brothers testing wing models in a small wooden wind tunnel

text: The Wrights built a small wind tunnel after concluding that existing lift tables were inaccurate. Source: National Park Service, The First Flight, https://www.nps.gov/wrbr/learn/historyculture/thefirstflight.htm

name: Section
text: THE FIRST FLIGHT

name: Slide title
text:
December 17, 1903
Kitty Hawk, North Carolina

name: Slide description
text: Orville piloted the first successful powered flight. The brothers made four flights that morning, improving their distance each time.
textPreview: Orville piloted the first successful powered flight. The brothers made four flights that morning, improving their distance each time.

name: Duration label
text: SECONDS

name: Distance label
text: FEET

alt: The Wright Flyer rising above its launch rail as Wilbur runs alongside

text: The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 120 feet; four powered flights took place that day. Sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, 1903 Wright Flyer, https://airandspace.si.edu/collection-objects/wright-1903-flyer/nasm_A19610048000; National Park Service, Four Powered Flights, https://www.nps.gov/places/3-four-powered-flights.htm

name: Section
text: THE ENDURING LESSON

name: Slide title
text:
Progress came from
learning what failed
textPreview: Progress came from | learning what failed

name: Slide description
text: They tested, measured, and redesigned before adding an engine. Careful evidence and steady iteration made controlled flight possible.
textPreview: They tested, measured, and redesigned before adding an engine. Careful evidence and steady iteration made controlled flight possible.

alt: The early Wright Flyer on the beach, with a modern airliner crossing the distant sky

text: The Wrights used wind tunnel research and flight testing as design tools, establishing a foundation for aeronautical engineering. Source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, 1903 Wright Flyer, https://airandspace.si.edu/collection-objects/wright-1903-flyer/nasm_A19610048000
